key_insight: Genotyping all detected malaria infections provided a more comprehensive assessment of CIS43LS efficacy than time-to-first-infection analysis, with improved precision in subgroup and monthly analyses.
clinical_relevance: For malaria prevention research—not AI cancer drug discovery—tracking new parasite strains can clarify protection across follow-up and assess potential antibody escape.
method: Genotyped all detected Plasmodium falciparum infections in a phase 2 trial involving 330 Malian adults.
Calculated molecular force of infection: the rate of newly acquired parasite strains.
Compared strain acquisition between CIS43LS and placebo arms and examined the antibody-targeted epitope for escape polymorphisms.
evidence_signal: Over six months, CIS43LS reduced molecular force of infection by 86.5% (95% CI: 80.1–90.8) at 40 mg/kg and 70.7% (61.0–78.0) at 10 mg/kg; no evidence of epitope escape polymorphisms was found.
watch_item: Findings from one six-month trial in Malian adults do not establish long-term protection or rule out escape in other populations.
paper_title: Genotypic infection endpoint analysis to understand efficacy and escape potential of the malaria monoclonal antibody CIS43LS
